plataforma-artes.name: Platform of Arts and Creativity
plataforma-artes.short: A 2012 Pitágoras complex in the old city market, home to the José de Guimarães museum
plataforma-artes.long: The Platform of Arts and Creativity is the transformation of Guimarães' old municipal market on Avenida Conde Margaride into a multifunctional space for creative work. The remodelling was carried out by the studio Pitágoras Arquitetos, and the complex opened on 24 June 2012, the year Guimarães was European Capital of Culture. The built area exceeds ten thousand square metres; the building has thirteen exhibition rooms over three floors, a 198-seat Black Box, a conference room, a bookshop, climate-controlled storage and work areas. It houses the International Centre for the Arts José de Guimarães (CIAJG), with African, pre-Columbian and ancient Chinese collections. The complex is run by the organisation A Oficina.
plataforma-artes.history:
The Platform of Arts and Creativity (Plataforma das Artes e da Criatividade) is an infrastructure project converting Guimarães' former municipal market into a multifunctional space dedicated to creative activity. It stands on Avenida Conde Margaride, one of the city's main streets, a short walk from Largo do Toural and the historic centre, and occupies more than ten thousand square metres.

The design is by the architecture studio Pitágoras Arquitetos. The International Centre for the Arts José de Guimarães (CIAJG), the core of the complex, opened on 24 June 2012 as part of “Guimarães 2012 European Capital of Culture”. The architecture of the CIAJG is a succession of volumes and contrasting surfaces; it answers the need to create spaces of different purpose, with thirteen exhibition rooms distributed over three floors. The tension between the volume of the building and the space of the square is resolved in the experience of the exhibitions, concerts and talks held here.

The museum is built around the collection of the artist José de Guimarães, gathered from objects of different periods, places and contexts and set alongside works by contemporary artists. It is organised in three nuclei: African art, pre-Columbian art and ancient Chinese art. In this way the museum proposes a kind of “remontage” of art history as a succession of echoes, and a new purpose for the museum — a place of wonder and reflection.

The building contains a Black Box seating 198 for performances of various kinds, a conference room, a bookshop, specialised climate-controlled storage and work areas. Since it opened, the complex has been managed and programmed by A Oficina, which also runs the Centro Cultural Vila Flor and the Casa da Memória de Guimarães. The project has won awards: the Detail Prize Award 2012, the Red Dot Design Award “best of the best 2013” and the Prémio Nacional de Reabilitação Urbana 2013; it reached the final list of 25 projects for the 2013 Mies van der Rohe Award and the Copper in Architecture Awards of the European Copper Institute.

It is important not to confuse the Platform of Arts with the Centro Cultural Vila Flor — they are different venues, even though both are linked to A Oficina and to the European Capital of Culture.

The old market on whose site the Platform rose was long the trading heart of the city; its iron structures and tall roofs were a landmark on Avenida Conde Margaride. The remodelling did not erase the memory of the place but folded a new building into the urban fabric: the project linked the square in front of the complex to the streets of the historic centre and brought a whole block back into use. Today it hosts exhibitions, concerts, conferences and the educational programmes of A Oficina, with a bookshop and café on the ground floor. The José de Guimarães collection includes African, pre-Columbian and ancient Chinese art set alongside works by contemporary artists, and it continues to grow. The Platform has become one of the main venues of Guimarães' cultural life and a notable point of contemporary architecture on the city map.

plataforma-artes.tip: A CIAJG ticket covers the permanent collection and temporary exhibitions; check opening hours on ciajg.pt (usually Tuesday to Sunday). The complex is on Avenida Conde Margaride, a 5–10 minute walk from Largo do Toural and the historic centre. Do not confuse it with the Centro Cultural Vila Flor, a separate venue at the other end of the city. Afterwards it is easy to walk back to the Toural and the Alfândega tower.
